newsitem.title: FRANCE: French wheat slips on EU export caution.
newsitem.headline: French wheat slips on EU export caution.

text.p: French wheat prices eased on Friday after the European Union reduced exports at its grain auction on Thursday, dealers said.
Rouen wheat for January delivery was quoted at 855 francs per tonne, down five from Thursday. Rouen barley was steady at 855 francs per tonne for February-March delivery as sellers remained scarce.

The EU's cereals committee issued licences to export 71,900 tonnes of soft wheat and 75,000 tonnes of barley. This was well below the 250,000-300,000 tonnes of wheat the industry says the EU needs to export each week to absorb its bumper crop.
Traders and officials have linked yesterday's surprise move to the dollar's rally and the fragile state of world prices.

But some traders said the EU decision was expected in the light of this week's cautious bids. And although the EU has tacitly buried an official link between French export prices and U.S. soft red winter wheat -- seen as an unrepresentative benchmark just now -- Brussels is unwilling to stray too far below U.S. values and risk straining trade ties with Washington, they said.
Operators said the Commission could be more generous next week on the back of recent sales contracts. France sold wheat this week to Morocco, Iraq and possibly Tunisia, they said.
It may also face pressure to come up with higher export refunds if world wheat prices continue to ease, despite the effects of a rising dollar that makes the EU more competitive.
"Each new contract indicates a new decline (in prices). It remains unclear if Brussels will follow (the world market)," one dealer said.
On Thursday, Tunisia bought 125,000 tonnes of wheat for an some $158 with freight, a price some traders considered cheap when compared with French fob values around $150 per tonne.

But although at least one of the 25,000 tonne cargoes was sold on a French basis, other traders said the bulk of the sale was on optional-origin terms and it was wrong to jump to conclusions about its value.
MATIF milling wheat futures were indicated at 881-883 Francs francs per tonne for May expiry but no trade was reported.

French cash grain prices exclude carrying charges of 3.64 francs per tonne which must be added for every half-month between August 1 last year and the delivery period in question. For example the carrying charge for first-half February is 47.26 francs per tonne. -- Paris newsrom +331 4221 5432
